advances: An attained local-minimum condition with an explicit common signed chart and nonnegative radial first-variation measures. The arbitrary compatibility setting does not assert that these signed directions exist.

proof:
The compressed groups of 0354aa9a30918591 have projected halfspaces
$$
G_i=\left\{w:\left(\sum_j\rho_{ij}v_{ij}\right)\cdot(w-z_i)\ge0\right\},
$$
where $z_i$ is the group anchor, $v_{ij}$ is the base normal, and the positive weights $\rho_{ij}$ sum to one and balance the continuous normals. At a covered base their caps cover the whole continuous plane. The group continuations keep these projected halfspaces fixed by keeping the weighted sum of actual cap thresholds fixed. Every continued group has a common cap mass $\tau_i$. The nondeep groups have a strict mass gap at the base parameter, so the maximum $\tau_i/M$ over the retained deepest groups is a touching upper comparison near the base parameter. In particular $Z$ is nonempty. This uses only the fixed-normal continuation and coverage conclusion of 0354aa9a30918591.

Write $-S_{ij}$ for the old threshold slope, and $B_{ij}$ and $M'$ for the linear cap and total shape terms. Applying the quantile differentiation of d3c5fb55ec5bc99d separately within each retained deepest group gives its response
$$
g_i=\sum_j\theta_{ij}B_{ij}-\beta M',\qquad
\theta_{ij}=\frac{\rho_{ij}/S_{ij}}{\sum_\ell\rho_{i\ell}/S_{i\ell}}.
$$
Here $g_i$ is $M$ times the normalized derivative at the old parameter. The touching upper comparison cannot decrease along any feasible direction. Since the parameter domain is open and the responses are linear, strict separation would give a direction with every $g_i$ strictly negative if zero were outside their convex hull. Thus there are $\pi_i\ge0$ summing to one such that $\sum_i\pi_i g_i=0$. The argument uses the compressed comparison directly, without requiring one retained group at every deepest base.

Fix $z\in Z$ and evaluate this identity on its normalized radial direction. A cap in a deepest group anchored at $z$ cannot contain $(z,x_z)$ strictly. Otherwise sliding it inward through this interior mark removes positive own-fiber volume, contradicting the genuine raw depth $\beta M$ there. Thus each such cap has nonpositive margin at $(z,x_z)$. Its group's positive weighted margins sum to zero on that plane, so each is zero. Its fixed-cap derivative is therefore $1/2$ in the given direction. All other fixed-cap derivatives are nonnegative by the first-variation measure hypothesis. The total derivative is one. If $\pi(z)$ is the sum of the $\pi_i$ for groups anchored at $z$, the identity yields $0\ge\pi(z)/2-\beta$. Summing over $Z$ gives $1\le2\beta|Z|$. Compression gives $|Z|\le h(P)$, and $(1+1/d)^d\ge2$ gives $\Gamma_d\le1/2$.

statement:
Let a finite nonempty base $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ carry positive compact convex $d$-fibers compatible with their lifted hull, $d\ge1$. Let $h(P)$ be the Helly number for traces of convex sets on $P$. Suppose the family is a local minimum of maximum normalized closed-halfspace depth $\beta$ in an open finite-dimensional parameter chart of actual compatible fixed-base families, locally Hausdorff-Lipschitz at the old parameter. Write $M$ for total volume. Select one actual critical circuit at a restricted maximizer of ambient mixed depth in each fiber, and retain a projected Helly subcover of at most $h(P)$ whole groups. Let $Z$ be the distinct anchors of the retained groups whose common raw cap mass is $\beta M$.

Assume for each retained deepest group that its actual cap mass has a joint first-order expansion at the old parameter and threshold, with linear shape term and strictly negative threshold derivative. Assume also that total mass has a first-order expansion in the same chart with a linear derivative. For every $z\in Z$ assume there is a signed direction in this same open chart that has total volume derivative one and is supported on fiber $z$. Its fixed-cap shape derivatives are given by a nonnegative first-variation measure on that fiber. The measure assigns half its mass to each central cap through a point $x_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$ of raw ambient mixed depth $\beta M$.

Then $\beta\ge1/(2|Z|)\ge1/(2h(P))\ge\Gamma_d/h(P)$, where $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$.
title: Compressed quantile half-mass Helly bound under signed radial directions
